source_name: Registr smluv – Pravni ramec (legal framework page)
why_relevant: Official statement of what must be published, thresholds (CZK 50,000 excl. VAT), the 30-day deadline, and the exclusions/redactions regime — including the banking-secrecy carve-out that directly limits visibility of bank-side contracts. Essential to bound coverage claims.

source_name: Zakon c. 340/2015 Sb. o registru smluv (zakonyprolidi.cz, with EN translation)
why_relevant: The statute itself, with an English rendering — needed to state precisely which entities are obliged, which contracts are exempt (incl. the banking-secrecy exemption in the bank-vs-obliged-person context), and the ineffectiveness/voidness consequence that makes this register unusually complete.

source_name: Registr smluv – Publikacni formulare (publication forms & metadata schema)
why_relevant: Defines the metadata fields publishers fill in (subject, value with/without VAT, department, counterparty identifiers, contract date). Determines exactly which fields we can rely on for filtering banking/payment contracts and which are free text and therefore noisy.

source_name: Registr smluv – Caste dotazy (FAQ, test environment testrs.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Operational FAQ covering publication mechanics, corrections, redaction and deletion. Explains edge cases (retroactive changes, withdrawn contracts) that determine how our stored copies must be reconciled over time.

source_name: portal.gov.cz – Registr smluv service pages (publication + information requests)
why_relevant: Citizen/entity-facing description of the register service and of the formal route for requesting information out of it (service S13944). Relevant if a needed record is redacted and we must decide whether a statutory information request is worth filing.

source_name: Individual disclosed banking contract PDFs on smlouvy.gov.cz (document layer)
why_relevant: The register stores the actual signed documents. Observed examples include Komercni banka current-account agreements with municipalities and a J&T Banka legal-entity banking-services agreement. These carry pricing schedules, terms, terminal/service annexes and redaction markers ('RED' = znecitelneno) — the real evidence layer for pricing and scope benchmarking.

source_name: zindex methodology wiki (wiki.zindex.cz) and EconLab VZMR methodology
why_relevant: Published methodology for scoring Czech contracting authorities across openness, competition and control — including how contract-register disclosure is used as an indicator. Gives us a defensible way to weight a buyer's transparency when interpreting missing banking contracts.

source_name: Municipal 'Registr smluv' pages on public-body websites (e.g. Praha-Dolni Mecholupy)
why_relevant: Many municipalities and districts maintain their own contract listing alongside the central register, sometimes with contracts below the CZK 50k threshold or with less redaction. Useful for filling gaps at the small-buyer end, where banking and terminal contracts are numerous but individually small.

source_name: epravo.cz – 'Seznamte se, registr smluv' article series (legal commentary)
why_relevant: Practitioner legal commentary on the exemptions regime, notably the banking-secrecy exemption and its limits when a bank contracts with an obliged entity. Directly bounds how much bank-side contract detail we can expect to see and why some banking contracts are absent or heavily redacted.

source_name: ARES – Administrativni registr ekonomickych subjektu
why_relevant: Authoritative ICO lookup for Czech legal entities. Required to build the banking/payments actor watchlist that drives every ICO-keyed query into the contract register and Hlidac, and to resolve name variants, mergers and branch entities of foreign PSPs.

source_name: Registr smluv entry page for CNB as a publishing party (example contract record)
why_relevant: Concrete example of a central-bank contract record in the register, showing the record structure (parties, subject, value, attachments) that our parser must handle. CNB is itself an obliged publisher, which makes central-bank IT/payments procurement partly visible here.

source_name: TENDER ARENA — profil zadavatele České dráhy, a.s. (Z0003016)
why_relevant: ČD is the single largest Czech state-owned buyer of ticketing/fare-collection and in-vehicle & counter payment acceptance (e-shop payment gateway, contactless EMV on board, POS at ticket offices). Its buyer profile publishes notices, ZD, clarifications (vysvětlení ZD) and award/contract data.

source_name: E-ZAK Správa železnic, státní organizace
why_relevant: Infrastructure manager (IČO 70994234, profile ID Z2020-000638), a sectoral contracting entity. Buys station retail/vending, parking payment, ticket-machine and treasury/banking-related services; also an anchor actor for the rail payments ecosystem.

source_name: E-ZAK / Tender Arena profil zadavatele — Letiště Praha, a.s. (Z0005204, IČO 28244532)
why_relevant: Prague Airport is a state-owned sectoral contracting entity and a heavy buyer of payment acceptance (parking, retail concessions, PRG e-shop, FX/DCC, treasury). It publicly announced migration from its own E-ZAK (zakazky.prg.aero) to Tender Arena — both must be tracked, the old one for historical awards.

source_name: Hlídač státu — Hlídač veřejných zakázek + Registr smluv mirror
why_relevant: Best aggregator/pointer for this cell: normalises VVZ + profiles + registr smluv per subject IČO, so one can enumerate every tender and contract of ČD, SŽ, Letiště Praha, DPP, hospitals, health insurers in one place, with an open API. Confirmed subject pages exist (e.g. IČO 70994234 Správa železnic, ico:28244532 Letiště Praha).

source_name: VZP ČR — Veřejné zakázky (largest Czech health insurer, buyer profile on Tender Arena)
source_subtype: contracting-authority procurement page + buyer profile pointer
why_relevant: VZP is the dominant health insurer and a major buyer of banking/payment-collection services (premium collection, payment traffic, card acceptance at branches). Its page states contracts are published in its buyer profile in Tender Arena; a separate profile exists for Pojišťovna VZP, a.s.

source_name: ZP MV ČR (211) — Veřejné zakázky, buyer profile on E-ZAKAZKY.CZ
why_relevant: Second-largest health insurer; procures under Act 134/2016. Its buyer profile is hosted on E-ZAKAZKY.CZ with downloadable tender documents, covering IT, postal and payment-collection related services.

source_name: Oborová zdravotní pojišťovna (OZP, 207) — buyer profile on E-ZAKAZKY.CZ
why_relevant: OZP (insurer of bank/insurance/construction employees) is a mid-size health insurer buyer; its full name literally names banking as its member base, and it procures collection/payment and IT services.

source_name: Skupina ČEZ — Výběrová řízení / Pro dodavatele
source_subtype: corporate supplier/procurement portal of state-controlled utility
why_relevant: ČEZ group is the archetypal Czech sectoral contracting entity; it states that its group companies publish sectoral contracts in the Věstník. Its own supplier pages (plus ČEZ Distribuce 'Nový dodavatel') describe the parallel non-statutory selection procedures where treasury, collection and customer-payment services would be sourced.

source_name: Dopravní podnik hl. m. Prahy (DPP) — procurement and contactless fare-payment programme pages
source_subtype: operator programme pages + press coverage of awarded contract
why_relevant: DPP is a municipally-owned sectoral transport operator and one of CZ's biggest acquiring merchants. Public reporting ties its ~1,200 in-vehicle/metro payment terminals to suppliers Bankovní informační technologie (ČSOB group) and Mikroelektronika with Mastercard, with a 6+2-year contract and revenue-share pricing — a directly comparable benchmark for payment-acceptance deals with state/municipal entities. Portal-vz.cz also lists DPP as a partner/contracting entity.

source_name: Dopravní podnik města Hradce Králové — EOC/ticketing modernisation tender pages (regional DP pattern)
why_relevant: Representative of the ~19 municipal transport undertakings (sectoral contracting entities) that each tender electronic fare collection including contactless bankcard clearing. These mid-size tenders are where payment-acceptance and clearing vendors actually compete, and they are usually announced on the operator's own site before/alongside the profile.

source_name: Obchodní věstník (ov.gov.cz)
why_relevant: Official commercial gazette with full-text search over corporate notices for entities such as České dráhy, a.s.; useful for corporate-event context (subsidiary formation, mergers of transport/utility subsidiaries) that reshapes who the contracting entity is and therefore who buys payment services.

source_name: Komerční banka – Všeobecné obchodní podmínky pro dodavatele (004)
why_relevant: The actual general terms a KB supplier signs up to. Gives contract mechanics — liability, subcontracting, audit rights, termination, information-security obligations — which is exactly the ground a bidder needs to price a bid and which reveals KB's risk posture toward outsourced IT/payments vendors.

source_name: ČSOB – Supplier Relations Policy / Politika vztahů s dodavateli (EN PDF)
why_relevant: ČSOB's own procurement policy document — the URL path itself contains 'procurement', indicating a dedicated procurement document tree under csob.cz/documents. Corroborating Czech-language coverage describes it as defining acceptable business practice for suppliers: conflict-of-interest elimination, anti-corruption, and mandatory acceptance of the ČSOB Group Ethical Code. This is the clearest published statement of how the largest CZ bank by assets governs vendor selection.

source_name: ČSOB Group Employee Code of Ethics (Etický kodex zaměstnanců skupiny ČSOB)
why_relevant: ČSOB's supplier policy makes acceptance of this code a condition of supplying the bank, so it is effectively part of the vendor onboarding pack. Useful for understanding gift/conflict rules that constrain how a vendor may approach ČSOB buyers.

source_name: Erste Group Procurement (EGP) – subsidiary and general supplier pages
why_relevant: Highest-value structural finding for Česká spořitelna. ČS does not run an independent public supplier portal; its external spend is managed by Erste Group Procurement, a Vienna-headquartered shared-service company with its OWN SUBSIDIARY IN THE CZECH REPUBLIC. EGP states it manages the whole external spend of all majority-owned Erste entities and splits activity into Sourcing (strategic, category/supplier management), Tactical Purchasing (low-value) and Order Management (call-offs from existing contracts) — a category-level map of how a ČS deal is actually routed. It also operates a standardised supplier onboarding process anchored on a Supplier Code of Conduct, and the general page offers supplier documents (Code of Conduct, General Terms and Conditions of Purchase) translated per country via a country drop-down, so a Czech-language ČS supplier pack should be reachable there.
